title: Documentation review prompt amendment
description:
Amend the documentation review prompt (`scripts/doc-review-prompt.md`) so a scope declared on an issue restricts review findings to that footprint, with full-surface review remaining the default when no scope is declared.

## Background

Documentation review today always covers the entire adopter-facing documentation surface: the prompt's enumerated "What you are reviewing" section lists the whole `docs/` tree plus the root adopter docs (`README.md`, `INSTALL.md`, `mcp-server/README.md`, `web/README.md`). An exhaustive documentation audit is splitting that surface into disjoint-footprint areas, each needing its own review restricted to its own footprint. Without a prompt change, every scoped review would report on the whole surface, drowning each pass in out-of-footprint findings and defeating the point of a narrow, per-area review. The review tooling already feeds the full issue context (including its description) to the reviewer ahead of the prompt text, so a scope declared in an issue's description reaches the reviewer with no change needed outside the prompt file itself.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The review prompt restricts findings to a description-declared file scope when present, and reviews the full surface when absent; behavior demonstrated by one scoped and one unscoped run.

## Notes

- Amend only `scripts/doc-review-prompt.md`: add a short "scoped audits" paragraph — when the context issue's description declares an audited scope (an explicit file/directory list), the reviewer restricts all findings to that scope; with no scope declared, it reviews the full surface exactly as it does today.
- The prompt's enumerated review surface is otherwise unchanged. Root `TESTING.md` is contributor documentation (it is relocating out of the adopter-facing surface as part of this audit's root-area work) and stays absent from the enumeration — this is correct, not an omission to fix.
- No change is needed outside the prompt file: the review tooling already passes the full issue context to the reviewer, so a description-declared scope reaches it as-is.
- Blast radius: `scripts/doc-review-prompt.md` only.
